report.source_text: In histopathology, the tumor is composed of spindle to epithelioid cells exhibiting marked pleomorphism with vascular growth pattern. Strange nuclei, giant nuclei, and multiple nuclei can be seen in tumor cells. Interspersed mitotic figures and areas of focal myxoid change and fibrinoid necrosis showed features of high-grade sarcoma. The immunohistochemistry results of tumor cells were positive for EMA, vimentin, and CD68, focally weakly positive for CR, SMA, ckp and bcl-2, and negative for WT1 and GFAP.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 26-year-old man presented with fever and dyspnea. Initial blood tests showed inflammatory activity with elevated WBC, CRP, D-dimer, and FDP. Chest enhanced CT revealed multiple filling defects in the main trunk and branches of the pulmonary arteries. Echocardiography demonstrated dilated right atrium and ventricle, impaired right ventricular systolic function, and abnormal echoes in the pulmonary artery and its branches. Doppler ultrasound detected lower extremity venous thrombosis. Histopathological examination of the pulmonary artery mass biopsy showed spindle to epithelioid cells with marked pleomorphism, mitotic figures, myxoid change, and fibrinoid necrosis, consistent with high-grade sarcoma. Immunohistochemistry was positive for EMA, vimentin, and CD68 among others, supporting sarcoma diagnosis. Postoperative enhanced CT scans of head, chest, and abdomen showed no evidence of other tumor tissues, confirming primary pulmonary artery sarcoma.
